job.title: Quantity Surveyor / Estimator - Civil & Earthworks
job.description:
With a growing workload and a strong pipeline of projects, our client is looking to bring another technically minded professional into their team. This is an opportunity for someone with a background in surveying, estimating or civil quantities to step into a varied role, work closely with experienced industry professionals and continue developing their skills.
  
With their head office located in Perth's southern suburbs, you’ll support projects across the Perth metropolitan area, working alongside engineers, project managers, clients and an experienced surveying team.
  
This isn’t just about filling a position. It’s about bringing the right person into the business, giving them the support they need and helping them build a long term future within the team.

The Role:
No two days will look exactly the same. You’ll be involved in both office based technical work and site visits, helping ensure quantities, project information and commercial requirements are accurately managed.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Completing quantity take offs, bills of quantities and estimating support.
  • Processing digital survey data and interpreting technical information.
  • Working with earthworks quantities, quarry materials and volume calculations.
  • Assisting with end of month (EOM) reporting and progress claims.
  • Reading and interpreting Australian construction specifications (AUSCONs).
  • Using software such as 12d, AutoCAD and Civil 3D to support project delivery.
  • Visiting sites across Perth to work with project managers on quantities, claims and project requirements.
  • Liaising with engineers, clients, contractors and internal teams to keep information accurate and projects moving.
  • Supporting multiple projects, with individual stages typically ranging from $3 million to $6 million.
About You:
We’re interested in someone who is comfortable working with numbers, has a good eye for detail and understands how accurate quantities and reliable technical information contribute to successful project delivery.

Ideally, you’ll bring:
  • Experience with quantities, take-offs, estimating or surveying related calculations.
  • Confidence processing digital information and working with technical data.
  • Some exposure to 12d, AutoCAD and/or Civil 3D.
  • An understanding of bills of quantities, progress claims and EOM reporting, or the ability to develop these skills.
  • The ability to interpret drawings, specifications and project documentation.
  • An understanding of bulk earthworks and quarry material volumes.
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to work with project managers, engineers and clients.
  • A practical approach to problem solving, with the ability to organise your workload across multiple projects.
On Offer
  • Genuine Monday - Friday 
  • Work locally, with a head office south of the river.
  • Company Vehicle and Fuel Card
  • Competitive Remuneration - starting from $110,000 plus Superannuation
  • Learn from experienced professionals and grow your career.
  • Take on responsibility, share ideas and build technical skills.
  • Work alongside an established team and with a strong project pipeline.
  • Building Industry relationships across the civil construction sector.
If you're ready for a career change, and to take the next step, and feel as though your skills and experience matches the selection criteria, please click apply or contact Reece Saldaris on Reece@designandbuild.com.au; for a confidential chat.

job.title: Automation Technician
job.description:
Industrial Automation Technologist / Technician

Location: Wetherill Park, Sydney
Industry: Advanced Manufacturing (Injection Moulding & Automation) Employment Type: Full-time, 24/7 manufacturing environment

About the Role
Our client, an established manufacturing operation based in Wetherill Park, is seeking an experienced Industrial Automation Technologist/Technician to join their team. This is a hands-on, technically diverse role supporting PLC-driven automation, industrial robotics, injection moulding machinery, and high-speed production equipment across a 24/7 site.

You'll be a key technical point of contact for production issues relating to equipment performance, product quality, and efficiency — working closely with Production, Maintenance, and Quality teams to minimise downtime and maximise OEE.
This role blends fault-finding, preventative maintenance, die setting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement, with genuine exposure to automation upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects.

Key Responsibilities
Automation & Technical Maintenance
  • Troubleshoot and maintain industrial automation and production equipment across a 24/7 environment
  • Service, repair, and set up injection moulding machines, industrial robots, IML systems, and auxiliary equipment
  • Fault-find and replace mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components
  • Integrate industrial robots into material handling, inspection, and packaging applications, including safety interlock verification
  • Perform preventative and predictive maintenance, equipment upgrades, and calibrations
  • Complete major equipment overhauls and support complex machine, processing, and die-setting issues
Production & Process Support
  • Act as a key technical contact for production issues affecting output, quality, reliability, and efficiency
  • Perform die, insert, and colour changes, including machine start-ups and shutdowns
  • Set, adjust, and optimise robotics, machine software, and production process parameters
  • Troubleshoot production faults, including IML and high-speed packaging equipment
  • Maintain target cycle times while ensuring finished products meet specification
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
  • Investigate recurring and new faults using structured root-cause analysis; implement corrective and preventative actions
  • Analyse downtime, rejects, defects, and waste to identify improvement opportunities
  • Support automation design, programming, commissioning, and equipment upgrades
  • Maintain accurate records of downtime, rejects, NCRs, maintenance activities, and corrective actions
Quality & Compliance
  • Work closely with Quality Assurance to ensure equipment and processes meet product, customer, and regulatory requirements
  • Ensure compliance with site quality systems, HACCP, and applicable food safety requirements
  • Verify new or modified automation systems before production handover
Safety & Team Support
  • Work in line with WHS legislation, site safety procedures, and permit requirements
  • Identify, report, and rectify hazards and near misses
  • Coordinate with third-party service technicians when required
  • Support training and technical upskilling of production and maintenance personnel
  • Communicate and escalate technical issues across shifts to maintain operational continuity
About You
  • Proven experience in industrial automation, robotics, and/or injection moulding within a manufacturing environment
  • Strong mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic fault-finding skills
  • Experience with PLC-driven systems and industrial robot integration
  • Die-setting experience highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, 24/7 production environment
  • Strong root-cause analysis and continuous improvement mindset
  • Food safety/HACCP exposure an advantage
  • Ability to train and support colleagues, and communicate effectively across shifts
Why Apply
  • Stable, full-time opportunity with genuine exposure to modern automation technology
  • Hands-on role combining automation, robotics, and process engineering — not a narrow, single-skill position
  • Real input into equipment upgrades and manufacturing improvement projects
  • Work within an established, well-resourced manufacturing operation

job.title: Foreman
job.description:
Working Foreman – Luxury Residential Construction Eastern Suburbs | Projects up to $3M | $125K+ Super
We are looking for an experienced Working Foreman to join our team and take a hands-on leadership role across a range of high-end residential projects in Sydney’s Eastern Suburbs.
Our projects are valued up to $3 million, with a strong focus on quality, attention to detail and delivering luxury residential builds to a high standard.
The Role As Working Foreman, you will be responsible for the day-to-day running of your projects, coordinating trades and ensuring works are completed safely, efficiently and to program.
You will be working hands-on where required while leading a team of subcontractors and carpenters on site.
Key Responsibilities
  • Manage the day-to-day operations of residential construction sites
  • Lead and coordinate subcontractors, carpenters and trades
  • Maintain high standards of workmanship and attention to detail
  • Coordinate trades and ensure projects remain on schedule
  • Read and interpret plans, specifications and construction documentation
  • Manage site materials, deliveries and logistics
  • Maintain a clean, safe and well-organised site
  • Liaise with project managers, clients, architects and consultants
  • Identify and resolve issues quickly and effectively
  • Assist with programming and planning upcoming works
About You We are looking for someone who:
  • Has solid experience as a Foreman or Working Foreman
  • Has proven experience delivering luxury/high-end residential projects
  • Has experience working on projects valued up to $3M
  • Can confidently run and coordinate a team of subcontractors and carpenters
  • Has strong knowledge of residential construction from start to finish
  • Takes pride in quality workmanship and presentation
  • Is organised, reliable and proactive
  • Can communicate effectively with trades, management and clients
  • Has a strong understanding of site safety and construction requirements
  • Is comfortable being hands-on and leading from the front
What’s On Offer
  • Salary up to $125,000 + Super, depending on experience
  • High-end residential projects throughout Sydney’s Eastern Suburbs
  • Stable pipeline of quality projects
  • Supportive and professional team environment
  • Opportunity to take ownership of projects and progress within the business
If you're an experienced residential Foreman who takes pride in delivering high-quality luxury homes and can confidently lead a site team, we'd like to hear from you. Email Tara on trogers@designandbuild.com.au

job.title: National Government Account Manager | Workplace Solutions
job.description:
Strategic Federal Government Accounts | National Role | Workplace Solutions

The Company
Our client is a long-established Australian organisation with a strong national presence, delivering high-quality workplace products and solutions to major organisations across Australia.

Due to continued growth, they are seeking an experienced National Account Manager – Federal Government to take ownership of strategic government relationships and drive long-term growth across the sector.

The Opportunity
This is a senior, strategic relationship role focused on building and growing relationships across Federal Government.

Rather than transactional or project-by-project sales, you’ll take a longer-term approach – understanding clients' national property and workplace portfolios, developing multi-year account strategies and identifying opportunities well before they formally come to market.

You’ll work with senior stakeholders across Property, Workplace, Facilities, Procurement, Design, People & Culture and Executive teams, while partnering with internal state-based teams to deliver a coordinated national approach.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Own and develop strategic relationships across key Federal Government accounts
  • Develop 1–3-year account and growth strategies
  • Protect and grow existing relationships while identifying new Federal Government opportunities
  • Build relationships with senior government decision-makers and influencers
  • Understand clients' national workplace and property strategies to identify future opportunities
  • Grow share of wallet across existing accounts
  • Develop and negotiate national agreements, rates and preferred supplier arrangements
  • Identify opportunities to introduce additional workplace products and solutions
  • Work closely with state sales teams to deliver a consistent national client experience
  • Maintain visibility of pipeline, account activity and future opportunities
  • Support major tenders and national procurement opportunities.
About You
This role requires someone who already knows the Federal Government market. You will bring established relationships and understand how to navigate complex government stakeholder and procurement environments.
Ideally, you will have:
  • An existing network/black book of Federal Government contacts
  • 5+ years' relevant sales, business development or account management experience at Federal Government level
  • Experience managing large, complex and strategic accounts
  • Strong relationships across government Property, Workplace, Facilities and/or Procurement functions
  • A track record of both growing existing accounts and developing new relationships
  • Experience developing long-term account strategies rather than simply pursuing individual projects
  • Strong commercial and stakeholder management capability
  • Confidence engaging with senior decision-makers
  • A strategic, relationship-led approach to business development
Previous experience introducing new products or solutions to market will also be highly regarded.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an established Federal Government account professional to take ownership of a significant national portfolio and build long-term relationships within an established Australian organisation.

For any questions relating to this role or other opportunities with D&B and our clients please contact Renee Hamilton at rhamilton@designandbuild.com.au or click apply. Your application will be treated as strictly confidential

job.title: Site Engineer
job.description:
Are you a mechanically minded Site Engineer with experience across water, wastewater or infrastructure projects?

Design & Build have partnered with a leading specialist in water and wastewater solutions to find an experienced Site Engineer for a contract opportunity in Brisbane.

Location: Brisbane, QLD
Type: Contract
Duration: Initial contract with potential for further work
Rate: Negotiable based on experience

About the Role:

As Site Engineer, you’ll support the delivery of water and wastewater infrastructure projects, working closely with the Project Manager, site team, subcontractors and design consultants.

The role will have a strong focus on site coordination, technical support, QA, documentation and ensuring works are delivered safely and to program.

Projects can include pump stations, odour control systems, water treatment assets and associated infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide engineering support across live construction projects
  • Review engineering and construction drawings for buildability
  • Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers and site activities
  • Assist with procurement and tracking of materials and equipment
  • Manage QA documentation including ITPs, ITCs and inspections
  • Raise and manage RFIs and technical queries
  • Assist with project programming, cost tracking and reporting
  • Monitor construction progress and ensure works are delivered to specification
  • Liaise with design teams, consultants, suppliers and project stakeholders
  • Provide hands-on engineering support during construction and commissioning
  • Ensure compliance with quality, safety and environmental requirements
About You
  • Degree in Mechanical, Civil or Environmental Engineering, or related discipline
  • 2+ years’ Site/Project Engineering experience
  • Experience within water, wastewater, civil or infrastructure projects highly regarded
  • Strong understanding of engineering and construction drawings
  • Experience with QA, ITPs, RFIs and site documentation
  • Confident coordinating subcontractors and working with site teams
  • Mechanically minded with strong problem-solving skills
  • Able to work across multiple work fronts and hit the ground running
  • Experience with 3D modelling software such as Inventor or SolidWorks highly advantageous
What’s on Offer
  • Contract opportunity with a specialist water infrastructure business
  • Brisbane-based projects
  • Exposure to a range of water and wastewater infrastructure projects
  • Hands-on site-based engineering experience
  • Potential for ongoing contract opportunities

What we’re looking for
